# BenchCAD census and reach curve

Generated by `uv run arris-gym census --corpus benchcad --out DIR` from
`BenchCAD/BenchCAD`, `code_gen`, revision
`5919f578ab09ec283603a082fab07c7639ab56eb`. No source programs are committed.
The 17,900 programs all parse. The aggregate census digest remains C1's
`043db6d912c7b77e4b0bc570b9160b2153286279f11a69ceccc57a63193d13ee`.

`programs.jsonl.gz` holds canonical JSON lines sorted by stem, with each
program's SHA-256, family, census outcome and corpus source, revision and
licence. Gzip has `mtime=0`. `reach.json` starts at 1,871/17,900 and admits
one missing census item (form, selector or end form) per step, greedily by
programs immediately unlocked, then by programs still missing it, then kind
and key. Seven forms reach 4,523/17,900 (25.27%); the first selector, `>Z`,
is the fifteenth item; twenty-four reach 9,061/17,900 (50.62%) and all 57
reach 17,900. Zero-gain items remain. `manifest.json` records the uncompressed rows' SHA-256 and the
validated census and reach digests. Two independent census runs give equal
bytes and digests. The current census marks 392 deferred polygon lofts
under ADR-0012, using `close()`'s endpoint tolerance when counting sides.
The annotated program rows regenerate with the census command. The
committed reach curve uses the frozen C1 subset in `tests/fixture_cases.py`
and is reproduced offline by `test_committed_benchcad_curve_repeats_offline`.

These counts and stems are adapted from [BenchCAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/BenchCAD/BenchCAD)
and shared under its [CC-BY-4.0 licence](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).


## The table

`fidelity.json.gz` compares all 17,900 programs under `cq` on arris 0.12.0
with the committed oracle rows from CadQuery 2.3.0 and Open CASCADE 7.9.3.0.
`arris-report.json` and `.md` describe the refusals and arris bugs.
`reach-report.json` checks the table against the census and `cq.subset()`.

Regenerate with the synced oracle environment and a fresh work directory
(outside the gate).

```sh
root=tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad
work=$(mktemp -d .scratch/benchcad-fidelity.XXXXXX)
uv run --locked --extra corpus tools/cq_corpus.py --corpus benchcad \
  --verdicts "$root/verdicts.json" "$root/loft-replay/verdicts.json" \
    "$root/loft-replay/trim-verdict.json" \
  --oracle-rows "$root/oracle.jsonl.gz" \
  --out-dir "$work/out" --work-dir "$work/chunks" --workers 16
```

Reach is 15,326/17,900 (85.6%), above the ADR-0014 target of 15,215.
Of all 17,900 programs, 12,523 agree and 5,377 disagree. The disagreement
classes are 372 `arris_bug`, 899 `arris_refusal`, 2 `by_design`, 2,573
`cq_bug` and 1,531 `occt_wrong`. There are zero unclassified rows, timeouts
and in-subset `cq_bug` rows. The two `by_design` rows are the vertex blends
from ADR-0025. All 392 deferred gear lofts remain in the table as
outside-subset `cq_bug` rows under ADR-0012 and ADR-0026.

Candidate statuses are 14,395 `ok`, 2,573 `unsupported_api`, 900
`arris_refusal` and 32 `checker_fail`. The pinned oracle has 17,568 `ok`
and 332 `invalid` reports.

The table digest is
`aa4fb6b6ea89276adc2c55b177e7b1a1bb1e31b42683dc79ceff0b7e673b94dd`.
The fresh replay reproduces the pinned oracle file byte-for-byte with
uncompressed SHA-256
`db298f073af368bc5a73f6856134cd0c8bcafa4bb3a9f6a7911de668fd49136b`.
The aggregate census and per-program rows also regenerate byte-for-byte.

### Changed classes after lofts, tapers and mirrors

The 1,176 newly reached programs were `cq_bug` before the lift. Every
other fidelity row is byte-identical to the pre-lift table's row.

| Outcome or class | Rows | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| Agreement | 832 | Both builds agree under ADR-0005. |
| `arris_refusal` | 129 | 117 classed by the comparison rule and 12 wing nuts whose corner refusals match the reduced regression. |
| `arris_bug` | 51 | 41 propellers and 4 gussets with excess bounds, 5 knobs and 1 wing nut. |
| `occt_wrong` | 164 | 145 knobs, 15 propellers, 3 I-beams and 1 gusset by analytic measures or boundary integrals. |

stems and their measurement gaps ahead of the next full table.

some runs and not on others: Open CASCADE's boolean, chamfer and shell order
depends on memory addresses (address-space layout and a job's position on its
zygote). No fidelity row moved (all 214 are the same as the baseline's, so the
table's digest does not depend on which oracle bytes are kept), so the baseline
rows stayed committed (BACKLOG Findings `oracle-nondeterministic-step`).

## The 717's diagnosis

`cq-bugs.json` archives a rerun of the baseline's 717 statically in-subset
`cq_bug` programs, from `uv run --extra corpus tools/cq_diagnose.py`.
The tool does not import or run the oracle. Every selected row retains its
stem, family, program SHA-256, status, message verbatim, versions, source and
CC-BY-4.0 licence; no program text or wall-clock value is stored. The
histogram counts every row, and names its families:

- `cq.Workplane('YZ')`: 319 programs.
- `cq.Workplane('XZ')`: 285 programs.
- `Workplane.circle on a non-empty stack`: 113 programs, all `torus_link`.

The constructor's string form admits plane values the implementation refuses;
the circles are drawn after `moveTo` puts a point on the stack. These are first
failures; later calls have not yet run. Shrunk strict-xfail regressions live in
`regression/cq-plane-yz`, `regression/cq-plane-xz` and
`regression/cq-circle-at-point`. No declaration is removed, so diagnosing the
failures does not change reach or the baseline table's digest above.

Two independent diagnosis runs give identical JSON bytes. The archive pins the
baseline table's digest (above); it remains that baseline's diagnosis now the
table is regenerated after the fixes: all 717 are in the subset and none is a
`cq_bug` row (604 agree, 70 `torus_link` agree, 43 `arris_refusal`). Attribution and licence are the
same BenchCAD CC-BY-4.0 attribution linked above.

## Verdicts

`verdicts.json` records 1,934 checked verdicts (ADR-0006). The
[loft replay](loft-replay/README.md) supplies 227 additional verdicts and
their evidence. `verdicts.args` includes the measured gaps and verified
failures from the 0.12.0 replay. Stems in the failure checks take precedence
over earlier family or stem flags. Regenerate from the repository root:

```sh
uv run --locked --extra corpus tools/cq_closed_forms.py \
  @tests/fixtures/c2/benchcad/verdicts.args
```

The generator checks each verdict against both builds. The form families,
deliberate differences and regression fixtures are specified by the
arguments and `tools/cq_closed_forms.py`. The file includes all 90 rivet
closed forms and replaces the historic cotter-pin and overlapping-chamfer
verdicts with the checked failure causes.
